transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Julian Park (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (CTO - Astra), Sara Gomez (ML Eng), Liam O'Connor (Infra)

Summary / Topics (auto):
- Latency targets (p95) for chat and batch summarization
- Concurrency and token/sec benchmarking
- Streaming + SSE support and client-side assembly
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (cost, SLOs, data residency)
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. This is Maya from Redwood, with Julian, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Ravi: Good thanks, Ravi here. Appreciate you fitting us in, we've got a few folks from infra and ML.
[00:09] Sara: Hi, Sara. We're excited to get into latency stuff.
[00:12] Julian: Great, quick agenda: understand your targets (p95), concurrency, streaming needs, then we'll map to hosted/dedicated/private options and propose a benchmark plan.
[00:20] Liam: Sounds good. Quick note, our infra team is sensitive about keys and auditability, so we'll need KMS + audit logs and maybe VPC peering for dedicated.
[00:28] Maya: Yep, that's common. We'll cover those. Maybe start with your product - what's the primary workload?
[00:33] Ravi: Two main flows: 1) in-app chat for drivers and dispatch - short prompts, expect many concurrent users; 2) nightly doc summarization for manifests, which are longer contexts, so throughput matters. For chat we want as close to realtime as possible.
[00:45] Sara: To add numbers: chat sessions average 120 tokens per response, sometimes up to 400. We expect steady state ~200 concurrent active users, peaks up to 500 concurrent. Nightly batch runs handle ~10k documents, average 2k tokens each but that's offline.
[01:05] Julian: Ok useful. What are your p95 SLOs today or target?
[01:08] Ravi: We don't have formal SLOs yet. Goal would be p95 <= 250ms for short chat responses, but we're flexible if that's unrealistic. For longer generation summaries p95 up to 2s is acceptable.
[01:20] Maya: 250ms p95 for 120 tokens is pretty aggressive, especially across open models and multi-tenant hosted infra. Can I ask about streaming - do you need token-by-token streaming to the client to appear realtime?
[01:31] Sara: Yes, streaming is required for chat UX. We use SSE for in-app. Latency perceived by user matters more than full-response latency. If streaming token arrives quickly, it's ok if full generation completes slightly later.
[01:44] Julian: Good - streaming changes the calculus. If we stream early tokens quickly, perceived latency drops. For token/sec benchmarking we'll measure time-to-first-token (TTFT) and p95 full-response.
[01:55] Liam: On infra, we'd prefer Dedicated if the sled (sic) - if the load is steady - means predictable costs. But we need to validate throughput: do you have recommended GPU types and batch sizes?
[02:05] Julian: For Dedicated we recommend A100 80GB or H100s depending on model and quantization. Batch size and sequence length affect throughput. For chat with streaming and small responses you often keep batch small to meet latency SLOs. We can provide quantized variants (Q4/Q8) for cost-saving; Redwood Dedicated supports automatic quantization profiles.
[02:24] Ravi: How about hosted? Is there a clear throughput guarantee?
[02:27] Maya: Hosted has published latency profiles but not firm per-customer throughput guarantees - it's multitenant. If you need firm p95 under load, Dedicated or Private is the way to go. We can route by region and use fallback models to gracefully degrade.
[02:40] Sara: Any examples of p95 numbers for 120-token responses on hosted?
[02:44] Julian: From our catalog benchmarks: for a 120-token response on popular open LLMs, median on hosted is ~80-200ms to first token depending on model and region; p95 is often 400-900ms without streaming optimization. With our streaming optimizations and prefix KV caching we can often cut perceived latency in half for repeated patterns.
[03:04] Ravi: Hmm ok. So realistically hosted probably can't meet our 250ms p95 target at scale.
[03:09] Maya: Many customers in similar situations start with hosted for dev and early prod, then move to Dedicated when they need predictable tail latency and consistent cost.
[03:16] Liam: For Dedicated, what's the concurrency per GPU? If we need 200 steady concurrent users, how many GPUs is that?
[03:22] Julian: Rough ballpark depends on tokens/sec and response length. Example: on an H100 with optimized kernels, for a short 120-token gen at typical configs you might get ~150-300 concurrent low-latency streams per GPU if using quantization and small batches. For safety we size conservatively - we can run a benchmark with your prompts to give concrete numbers.
[03:42] Sara: We definitely want that benchmark. Also want to confirm streaming SDKs - do you support SSE/Websockets and function/tool calling?
[03:50] Maya: Yes, SDKs and streaming via SSE + websockets are supported. We also have function-calling features and structured output. We'll include links in the follow-up.
[03:58] Julian: One more note: caching helps a lot for repeated queries. If drivers frequently ask the same route questions, prefix/KV caching can drop p95 by up to 40% for those queries.
[04:10] Ravi: Good point. For metrics, we care about p95 and tokens/sec at peak. We can provide a token-length distribution.
[04:18] Sara: I'll attach the CSV with token distribution and our RPS curve. That will help the benchmark.
[04:22] Liam: Security: how do you handle keys and audit? We need KMS integration, customer-managed keys, and audit logs stored for 1 year.
[04:30] Maya: For Dedicated/Private we support KMS/HSM integrations and full audit logs. Hosted has enterprise plans with customer-managed keys and extended audit retention as an add-on. We'll share the SOC 2 and ISO docs.
[04:42] Ravi: Any network options? VPC peering?
[04:45] Julian: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. Private on-prem is also possible if you need air-gapped.
[04:52] Sara: Back to latency - can you run time-to-first-token tests? We care about TTFT under cold start and warm conditions.
[04:59] Julian: Absolutely. Our benchmark plan will include TTFT, p50/p95 for full response, throughput (tokens/sec) under concurrent streams at steady and burst loads. We'll test hosted and Dedicated variants with your prompt set. Also measure streaming frame latency.
[05:16] Maya: We'll propose a short pilot: 2-week benchmark with your prompts on hosted and a small Dedicated pool (1-2 GPUs). We'll collect data and iterate.
[05:24] Ravi: Cost sensitivity - what's the incremental cost to get p95 down? Are there knobs we can turn?
[05:29] Julian: Knobs: move to Dedicated (predictable), use quantized models, enable KV/prefix caching, tune batch windows, and use smaller model variants for trivial prompts. Each reduces cost but has tradeoffs for quality and latency. We'll show estimated unit economics in the pricing doc.
[05:44] Liam: Any pitfalls on the Dedicated side? Ops overhead?
[05:47] Maya: We manage the control plane; Dedicated customers get an SLA and we handle runtime updates. You get access to the console for tracing, per-token cost, and rollouts. Private on-prem is heavier, we provide an image and support but it's more hands-on.
[06:02] Sara: For data residency - our EU regs require logs to remain in EU. Is that supported?
[06:06] Julian: Yes, Dedicated/Private can be deployed to specific regions and logs kept there. Hosted has region controls but you'd want Dedicated for strict residency guarantees.
[06:15] Ravi: Ok let's talk specifics of the benchmark. If we provide a 24-hour traffic trace plus 1000 prompt examples, can you run a scaled test?
[06:23] Julian: Yes, we'll do synthetic load to replicate peaks. We prefer sample prompt set + trace. We'll test both streaming and non-streaming modes, and include model variants and quantization.
[06:34] Sara: Can you also test fallback behavior? For example, if dedicated capacity hits a limit, do requests fall back to hosted or smaller model?
[06:41] Julian: Yes, Redwood has smart routing and fallback policies - we can configure route by latency, cost, region, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. We'll include that in the runbook.
[06:52] Maya: Next steps recap - Maya sends pricing and SLA docs, Julian shares benchmark plan + sample prompts, Sara provides traffic/profile. Schedule follow-up demo of Dedicated.
[07:03] Ravi: Sounds good. Any risks we should be aware of?
[07:06] Julian: Main risk is target p95 of 250ms for 120 tokens at scale - we'll validate with the benchmark. If we can't meet it with Dedicated, we can explore streaming-first UX and caching to lower perceived latency.
[07:19] Sara: That works. Also want to see token/sec numbers from the run - especially how it behaves under spikes.
[07:25] Maya: We'll include burst capacity options and autoscaling policies in the proposal.
[07:30] Liam: Cool. Thanks everyone. We'll aim to get the artifacts to you in 24-48 hours.
[07:35] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
